lesson_title: Eleven Slips, Six Doors: Running the Whole Books
hook_text: Eleven pieces of paper. Six doors. Under two minutes. That's real bookkeeping.
clip_script: Month-end evening at Zanele's Traders. She empties the document tray onto the counter: till slips, two invoices, a debit note, a bank deposit book, and one sad letter confirming Khumalo will never pay. Eleven pieces of paper. In the back room, six doors. The entire job of bookkeeping is getting every paper through its right door — and each door only asks simple questions. Did money come in? Did money go out? Goods out on trust? Goods in on trust? Anything travelling backwards? And the letter — no money, no goods — slips through the odd-jobs door with its explaining sentence. Eleven papers, well under two minutes. Two questions asked eleven times — not eleven procedures memorised.
visual_style: Top-down counter shot: papers gliding one by one through six glowing doorways, a stopwatch running, the sad letter drifting to a small seventh slot at the end.
pacing: Paper-per-beat rhythm accelerating to the stopwatch's stop.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and run a whole month to a level trial balance.
